title: Helm release stuck after operator upgrade — incident response, config drift reconciliation, and customer hotfix deployment
creator: Lena Park
description: Several customers running Private (VPC/on-prem) reported failed operator upgrades where Helm remained in a 'pending-upgrade' or 'failed-hook' state and the operator reconciliation loop stopped applying subsequent changes. Symptoms observed across multiple clusters: helm release pending due to a pre/post upgrade hook that never completed, operator pod entering CrashLoopBackOff after CRD validation errors, and configmaps/opaque secrets diverging between control plane intent and node-level state. Impact: customer-facing control plane features degraded, unable to deploy model revisions or scale worker pools. This ticket coordinates incident response, manual hotfix deployments for affected customers, and a durable fix to Helm/operator upgrade flow to prevent config drift and stuck releases.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start from operator v2.7.x with custom Helm values (custom tolerations + a pre-upgrade hook implementing DB migration).
2) Trigger a helm upgrade to operator v2.8.0 with changed CRD validation schema and an updated hook image.

3) Observe helm upgrade hang: pre-upgrade hook pod starts but never exits (waiting on mount/cert rotation task), helm shows 'pending-upgrade', operator controller encounters validation failures when reconciling existing CRs.
4) ConfigMaps generated by the operator diverge from what helm expects (immutable keys changed), causing subsequent helm upgrades to error with 'cannot patch immutable field'.
mitigation: 1) Run targeted remediation playbook for affected customers: mark upgrade as blocked in console, open support case and schedule maintenance window.
2) For stuck Helm releases: kubectl delete pod <hook-pod> to let hook failfast, then helm rollback --namespace <ns> <release> to last known-good revision.
3) If rollback fails due to immutable fields on ConfigMap: create a temporary rename of conflicting ConfigMap keys, perform rollback, then reconcile and migrate keys back safely.
4) For operator CrashLoopBackOff: scale operator deployment to 0 then back to 1 with patched env var to disable hook execution (FEATURE_UPGRADE_HOOKS=false) while we recover cluster.
5) Notify customers of root-cause and ETA; provide per-customer remediation notes and follow-up validation steps.

6) Create a short-lived hotfix (operator-2.8.1-hotfix) that disables non-idempotent hooks and includes migration idempotency guards; ship as patch per-customer via Helm --set image.tag=operator-2.8.1-hotfix.
7) Use the rollout-observer dashboard to validate operator heartbeat and reconciliation metrics before closing the incident.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Lena Park: Ticket opened after escalations from three enterprise customers in APAC and NA. Initial triage points to pre-upgrade hook deadlocks combined with CRD schema changes.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Alvarez: Confirmed that two clusters had helm releases stuck in pending-upgrade. Repro on staging with operator v2.8.0 and identical values showed same hang. Collected pod logs from hook container: it was blocked waiting on a KMS credential refresh that failed under the new startup ordering.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Priya Rao): Performed manual rollback for customer A using helm rollback; required renaming an immutable ConfigMap to bypass patch error. Documented steps in runbook link. Cluster health returned to green after operator scaled back up with FEATURE_UPGRADE_HOOKS=false.

2026-03-12 - Mateo Alvarez: Drafted hotfix operator-2.8.1 that disables legacy hooks by default and introduces a safe migration wrapper for DB migrations. PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1342.
2026-03-13 - Design (Aisha Chen): Reviewed customer-facing outage communication draft. Approved technical summary and rollback guidance. Adding link in support cases.

2026-03-14 - Mateo Alvarez: Hotfix v2.8.1 tested on canary cluster; helm upgrade with --wait succeeded. Preparing per-customer rollout plan; will coordinate maintenance windows and an automated preflight check before attempting upgrades.
2026-03-14 - Lena Park: Marking follow-ups: add telemetry for hook duration, fail-open behavior for KMS refresh, and unit tests for CRD schema migrations. Assigning long-term tasks to backlog.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotfix operator-2.8.1 is validated on canary and applied to all affected customers with documented rollback steps.
2) A short-term runbook exists and is attached to customer cases (includes kubectl/helm commands, known edge cases, and validation checks).
3) Post-release monitoring shows operator reconciliation heartbeat within SLO (>=99.9% over 1h) and no new stuck helm releases in 72h across sampled customers.
4) Two follow-up engineering tasks created: automated preflight validations for helm upgrades, and an operator-level safe-rollback feature; both have owners and estimates.
next_steps: 1) Complete PR review and merge for operator-2.8.1-hotfix (owner: Mateo).
2) Coordinate per-customer hotfix rollouts with Solutions Eng and Support; schedule maintenance windows and confirm backups.
3) Add a lightweight pre-upgrade preflight job that validates CRD compatibility and checks for immutable field changes; include as --check step in the console upgrade flow.
4) Instrument helm/operator metrics: hook_duration_seconds, operator_reconcile_errors_total, helm_release_stuck_count and add alerts for >1 stuck release per region in 30m.
5) Draft a post-incident blameless report and circulate to Eng/Product/SRE within 72 hours; include timeline, RCA, and follow-ups.
